section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "zemirot" means praise of the Torah, as Dovid praised the Torah by saying all worlds' vitality depends on one of its details, and also means cutting down, as through Torah study Dovid's enemies were nullified, and these two meanings are connected.
section.t: And the explanation is,
that "zemirot" is also a matter of praise.
As it is brought in Tanya,
that what Dovid called words of Torah by the name "zemirot" is the matter of praise of the Torah.
For Dovid would praise the Torah in that the vitality of all worlds depends on one detail of the details of the Torah.
And the connection of this explanation to the simple explanation of "Your statutes were my songs" etc.,
is,
that through contemplation on the greatness and praise of the Torah, that all worlds are nullified in existence relative to one detail of the details of Torah,
through this he effected in himself that all worldly matters would not occupy a place for him,
and even when it was not good for him in physicality,
he would engage in Torah with great joy.
And in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah
he explains yet another explanation of "Your statutes were my songs,"
"zemirot" is from the term cutting and severing,
like "to cut down tyrants."
For through the Torah study of King Dovid,
all his enemies and pursuers were nullified.
And as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"Rise early and stay late over them in the study hall, and they will be consumed of their own accord."
And one can connect the two explanations,
that through engaging in Torah in the manner of "zemirot" as per the explanation in Tanya,
that it was felt by him that the vitality of all worlds depends on
(one detail of)
Torah,
through this it came about,
that that which is not in accord with Torah,
and all the more so that which opposes Torah,
will have no vitality,
"zemirot" from the term "to cut down tyrants."
And based on this, it will also be understood what is said, "Your statutes were my songs"
(specifically "Your statutes"),
for the two matters mentioned above in the "zemirot" of Torah
(praise of the Torah,
and cutting down tyrants),
they are,
primarily,
from the aspect of the matter of the statutes (chukim) in the Torah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two general categories of mitzvos—those with reason (mishpatim) and those beyond reason (chukim)—correspond to two general aspects in divine service: service with reason and knowledge, and service with acceptance of the yoke, which must be present in every mitzvah.
section.t: And the explanation is,
that the two general divisions in the mitzvos,
mitzvos of testimonies and judgments that have a reason, and mitzvos of statutes that are above reason,
they are two general matters in divine service,
the service of reason and knowledge
(judgments)
and the service of acceptance of the yoke
(statutes),
which must be in every single mitzvah.
And the explanation is,
that in mitzvos there are two matters.
One,
that the mitzvos are His will, blessed be He,
a will that is above reason.
For this matter is in all mitzvos equally.
And two,
that after the will becomes clothed in wisdom
(of Torah),
behold, through this a reason is added to each mitzvah,
and also that through each mitzvah a particular light and revelation is drawn down.
For this is what [is meant by] the 248 commandments are the 248 limbs of the King,
for each limb is a vessel for a particular power.
And these reasons are from the aspect of the wisdom of Torah as it is above.
And from this were drawn down
(through the multiplicity of descent)
the reasons for the mitzvos that are in the revealed part of Torah
(the reasons of testimonies and judgments as they are simply).
And this is what [is meant] that in the fulfillment of mitzvos there must be two intentions,
a general intention and a particular intention,
that from the aspect of the will
(which is above reason)
there must be the general intention
(acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven)
to fulfill the will of G-d,
and from the aspect of the matter of the reasons of the mitzvos there must be the particular intention relevant to that mitzvah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of statutes and judgments are general principles in every mitzvah and in all of a person's conduct, where judgments involve judging everything according to Torah wisdom and statutes involve the constant service of accepting the yoke of Heaven.
section.t: And this is what [is meant] that the two matters of statutes and judgments are two general matters in every single mitzvah.
For even the mitzvos of testimonies and judgments that have a reason must be fulfilled
(primarily)
because they are the will of G-d,
like the statutes.
And likewise conversely,
that even in the mitzvos of statutes there is the reason and particular intention in them,
[namely] that through each mitzvah
(even the mitzvos of statutes)
a particular light and revelation is drawn down.
And furthermore,
that each of these two matters
(statutes and judgments)
is a general matter in the service of man,
not only in the fulfillment of mitzvos but also in the entire conduct of man.
For the matter of judgments is
(as explained in the maamar)
to judge every matter,
whether it is in accord with the intellect and wisdom of Torah,
and even when the matter in itself has no trace of prohibition,
one must weigh carefully whether it will not cause weakness in some mitzvah or custom of Israel,
in which case one must reject the matter entirely.
And the matter of statutes is the service of acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven,
which must be not only at the time of fulfilling a mitzvah but throughout the entire day.
